top_violation_types.title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §744.201(1))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Completed policied were not available during the inspection.

top_violation_types.title: Documented Annual Training-Required Topics in Health and Safety (26 TAC §744.1309(d))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: One caregiver was missing the required annual training in the following topics: 1309(C),  1309 (D) (2), 1309 (D) (3), 1309 (D) (4).

top_violation_types.title: Required Personnel Records (26 TAC §744.901)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: One caregiver didn't have their file available during the inspection.

top_violation_types.title: Children's Records Maintained (26 TAC §744.603(a))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: There was a child in care at the time of the inspection who did not have any records. The child also had a known allergy.

top_violation_types.title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §744.1205(a)(4))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Based on the information gathered during the investigation, it has been determined that child was left unattended, and caregiver was not at a physical proximity which did not allow visual and/or auditory awareness of the child in care.

top_violation_types.title: Policies Comply with Rules (26 TAC §747.207(1))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operation does not have written policy for procedures for the release of children, illness and exclusion criteria, procedures for dispensing medication a statement that medication is not dispensed, procedures for handling medical emergencies, discipline and guidance policy, safe sleep for infant 12 months old or younger, the procedures for parents to visit the child-care home any time during your hours of operation to observe their child, program activities, the home, the premises, and equipment without having to secure prior approval, the procedures for parents to review copy of the child-care home's most recent Licensing inspection report and how the parent may access the minimum standards online, instructions on how a parent may contact the local Licensing office, access the Texas Abuse and Neglect Hotline, and access the DFPS website your emergency preparedness plan, procedures for conducting health checks.

top_violation_types.title: Child/ Caregiver Ratio - Registered Child Care Home (26 TAC §747.1701)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The primary caregiver had seven students in care ages 3, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, and 22 months old. The operation was out of ratio by one student.

top_violation_types.title: Training Requirements for Primary Caregiver -30 Hours Annual Training (26 TAC §747.1303(5)(A))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Provider could not provide annual training hours during inspection.
